clue.text: Method analyst uses cunningly as I recite on sofa?

indicators.note: doing something cunningly means artfully contriving it, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient on the psychoanalyst's couch wonders whether reciting things is part of the therapist's technique.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder itself describes the scene: the patient on the couch reciting whatever comes to mind, which is the technique itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Free association is the Freudian technique in which a patient voices thoughts unfiltered, a standard tool of the psychoanalyst.

clue.text: Boaster's baronet trapping badger with fish

indicators.note: trapping means holding something inside, so the baronet's letters close around what follows

blocks.note: Bt is the standard abbreviation for baronet
to badger and to rag both mean to tease or pester
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A bragging aristocrat shows off having caught a badger along with some fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning to pester; 'Boaster's' is 'Boaster is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A braggart is a person who habitually brags, exactly a synonym for someone who boasts.

clue.text: Hot body that finally squeezes into short dress

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word it qualifies, keeping only its closing letter
something short has been cut, so the garment's name loses its last letter
squeezing into something means getting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the last letter of that
a sari is a draped dress worn in South Asia

explanation.surface: An attractive person with a hot body squeezes into a skimpy dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot body' suggests a glamorous figure, but it is an astronomical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a luminous ball of burning gas, so an intensely hot celestial body.

clue.text: Neanderthal perhaps appearing in romance stories

indicators.note: appearing in says the word turns up inside the text that follows, spanning its words

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A caveman character turns up in historical romance novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Neanderthals are early humans, and 'perhaps' marks them as an example of forebears from long ago.

clue.text: Several cheer falsely for Shadow Chancellor

indicators.note: falsely means not truly or in a distorted way, so these letters are put into a different order

blocks.note: twelve letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Several party members cheer insincerely for the opposition's finance spokesperson.
explanation.walkthrough: Rachel Reeves was Labour's Shadow Chancellor of the Exchequer, the opposition's spokesperson on the economy, before becoming Chancellor in 2024.
explanation.definitionFit: The Labour politician held the opposition post shadowing the UK finance minister when this puzzle appeared.

clue.text: Stalls around a square in the hills

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the stalls word encloses the other piece

blocks.note: pens are stalls or enclosures for animals
nine is a square number, three times three

explanation.surface: Livestock pens arranged round a village square somewhere up in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A square' is a square number, not a town square. The Pennines are the hill range forming the backbone of northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pennines are a range of upland hills running down northern England, so they are 'the hills' in a definite sense.

clue.text: See 5
Muscle was wasted with author finding substantial growth

indicators.note: wasted means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer's muscle has wasted away, but he has gained something substantial elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substantial growth' sounds like a tumour or a business result; it is facial hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A walrus moustache is a thick, drooping one covering the mouth, a notably bushy growth of facial hair.

clue.text: Fairy shown with Capek's play for first time in mythical place

indicators.note: putting one thing for another means swapping it in, and first says which occurrence is replaced

blocks.note: Titania is the fairy queen in A Midsummer Night's Dream
R.U.R. is Karel Capek's 1920 play that introduced the word robot
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A fairy appears alongside a Czech play staged for the first time in a fabled land.
explanation.walkthrough: The first T of the fairy queen's name is replaced by the play's title. Ruritania is the invented kingdom of Anthony Hope's The Prisoner of Zenda.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is a fictional Central European kingdom from Anthony Hope's novels, so an imaginary land rather than a real one.

clue.text: People in A&E taking turn, getting behind procedure

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, here the people within the hospital department letters
taking a turn means turning round, so the whole result is read backwards

blocks.note: A&E is the British hospital accident and emergency department, giving its two letters
men are people

explanation.surface: Patients in the emergency department take turns waiting for an unpleasant procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital emergency room. 'Behind procedure' means a procedure for the behind.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema injects fluid into the rectum, a medical procedure carried out on the backside.

clue.text: Ready with foil, almost finished wrapping cloth round

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of that word is dropped
turned round means facing the other way, so the cloth word is read backwards
wrapping something means enclosing it, so the first piece goes around the second

blocks.note: ended means finished
a rag is a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Something nearly done is being wrapped in cloth and kitchen foil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foil' looks like kitchen foil but is the fencing sword; en garde is the call to take guard in fencing.
explanation.definitionFit: En garde is the fencer's call to take the guard position, so a fencer holding a foil is ready for a bout.

clue.text: Drinker's comeuppance having to abandon grand city

indicators.note: abandoning something means leaving it behind, so one letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: the morning-after misery a drinker brings on themselves
G is short for grand, slang for a thousand

explanation.surface: A boozer gets his just deserts and must leave a great city.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanover (Hannover) is a major city in northern Germany, capital of Lower Saxony.

clue.text: One does associate with hunters at last catching game

indicators.note: at last points to the end of the preceding word, keeping only its final letter
catching means holding, so the single letter closes around the game word

blocks.note: the last letter of hunters
tag is a children's chasing game

explanation.surface: Someone who mixes with hunting folk finally gets drawn into a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like the verb but is the plural of doe, female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is a male deer, the animal that keeps company with female deer in the herd.

clue.text: Hardliners in way: mountain climbers leaving quietly

indicators.note: leaving means going away, so the letter for quietly departs from the climbers word

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
alpinists are mountaineers
p is the musical marking piano, quietly

explanation.surface: Uncompromising types stand in the way while mountaineers slip off without a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalinists follow Stalin's rigid, authoritarian line, so they are the archetype of political hardliners.

clue.text: Unsuitable party men not in the House?

blocks.note: out as in out of the question, unacceptable
a do is a party
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Politicians unfit for party office who failed to win a seat in the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital H makes it the House of Commons; really it is any house. OR, other ranks, is the crossword's usual source for 'men'.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor describes what takes place outside, i.e. away from the inside of a house or building.

clue.text: Work doubled with an American chopper used for tree

indicators.note: doubled means the work abbreviation is written twice in a row

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
the same abbreviation again
taken as written
ax is the American spelling of axe

explanation.surface: An American axe is used twice over to fell a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Opopanax is a rare word: a fragrant gum resin, and also the name of a small acacia tree that yields it.
explanation.definitionFit: Opopanax is the name of a thorny acacia shrub or small tree, a dictionary sense alongside the resin.

clue.text: Brutal police make move, seizing criminal tapes

indicators.note: criminal implies being bent or crooked, so those letters are scrambled
seizing means grabbing hold of, so the move word goes around the other letters

blocks.note: to go is to make a move in a game
taken as written

explanation.surface: Heavy-handed police move in and confiscate incriminating recordings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was Nazi Germany's secret state police, notorious for its brutality.

clue.text: What's taken up as challenge, but punishing for runners?

blocks.note: first meaning: the glove thrown down and picked up to accept a challenge
second meaning: the double line of attackers someone is made to run between

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses come from idioms: to take up the gauntlet, and to run the gauntlet, an old punishment of running between rows of men striking you.
explanation.definitionFit: The armoured glove thrown as a challenge and the ordeal of running between two lines of attackers share one name.

clue.text: Fellow about to be saved by a drunken medic

indicators.note: drunken means staggering and disordered, so the letters of the doctor word are jumbled
being saved by something means being held safe within it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
ca is circa, Latin for about
taken as written

explanation.surface: A college fellow is about to be rescued by a tipsy doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' looks like any man but means a member of a college's teaching staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow of a university college is a senior scholar, so an academic in the university sense.

clue.text: Our lingo is outrageously disgraceful

indicators.note: outrageously suggests wild and unruly behaviour, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the way we talk nowadays is shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Inglorious means bringing shame or dishonour, a straightforward synonym for shameful conduct.

clue.text: Butcher's chestnut horse turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from the bottom upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: chestnut is a reddish-brown colour
a nag is a horse

explanation.surface: A meat seller's old chestnut horse has shown up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher's' is Cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook = look. It is not the meat trade at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for a quick look: have a butcher's and have a gander mean the same.

clue.text: Like ring topped with cool blue

indicators.note: in a down clue being topped with something means having it placed above, so that piece is written first

blocks.note: in means fashionable, cool
to dig is slang for to like
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A ring with a cool blue stone set on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep violet-blue colour, the dye and shade between blue and violet in the spectrum.

clue.text: Pressure applied to idiot: "I don't know the answer"

blocks.note: p is the symbol for pressure
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A quizmaster leans on a dim contestant, who just admits not knowing.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted phrase is the definition in full: what a quiz contestant says when stumped.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'pass' on a quiz show declines a question, the stock way of admitting ignorance of the answer.

clue.text: Local vessel managed single-handedly?

blocks.note: surface reading: a boat on a nearby waterway sailed by one person alone
setter's reading: a drinking mug in a pub, the local, which has a single handle to grip

explanation.walkthrough: A local is a neighbourhood pub, and 'vessel' is a container for drink, not a boat; 'single-handedly' hints at its one handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large one-handled drinking mug, typically for beer, found in pubs.

clue.text: Starter of Taleggio: a fine cheese in thin cloth

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of Taleggio
taken as written
f is the pencil grade abbreviation for fine
feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: A cheese course begins with Italian Taleggio and some fine Greek cheese wrapped in muslin.
explanation.walkthrough: Taleggio is a soft Italian cheese, which makes the cheeseboard picture convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, fine-woven silk or synthetic fabric, a lightweight dress material.

clue.text: The Scandinavian Huckleberry?

blocks.note: first meaning: a native of Finland, loosely counted as Scandinavian
second meaning: the surname of Mark Twain's boy hero

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks whether there is a Nordic variety of the huckleberry fruit; the question mark signals that Huckleberry is the character's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Finn is a person from Finland, and Huckleberry Finn is Mark Twain's title character.

clue.text: Symbol of resistance from duck alongside Titanic

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, O
mega means huge, titanic

explanation.surface: A resistance emblem made from a duck shown beside the sunken liner.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital-T 'Titanic' looks like the ship but means enormous. In physics the Greek letter omega marks the ohm, the unit of electrical resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital Greek omega is the physics sign for ohms, the unit in which electrical resistance is measured.

clue.text: Riotous cheering around West London region

indicators.note: riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters of the cheering word are thrown about
around means surrounding, so the jumbled letters enclose the compass point

blocks.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: Wild cheering breaks out across a district of west London.
explanation.walkthrough: Greenwich is a borough in south-east London, home of the Royal Observatory and the prime meridian.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenwich is a London borough on the Thames, so a district of the capital.
